name: Venus
tagline: Earth's twin in size, wrapped in a crushing CO₂ greenhouse — the hottest planet.
history: Venus spins backwards and so slowly that its day outlasts its year. Beneath unbroken sulfuric-acid clouds, a runaway greenhouse keeps the surface near 465 °C — hot enough to melt lead — under 92 atmospheres of pressure. The Soviet Venera program achieved the first landings on another planet here between 1970 and 1982; no probe survived more than two hours. NASA's Magellan orbiter radar-mapped 98% of the surface between 1990 and 1994, revealing a volcanic world resurfaced as recently as a few hundred million years ago. Venus is often called Earth's evil twin: same size, similar rock, radically different fate — a cautionary tale in planetary climate.
